criteria.requirement: A node that loses one path to the LUN under load keeps working on the other; when the lost path returns it is reinstated and carries the I/O when the path that survived is lost in turn. No operation fails on any node, no node is fenced or stops, no lock is granted twice, and every acknowledged file is intact.
criteria.detector: tests/mpath/path_failover.sh (host-coordinated; F1 and F2 of docs/mpath-verification.md): every node runs tests/mpath/pathload.py (fsynced checksummed files, shared-directory churn, a mkdir mutual-exclusion witness); the last node's path on storage network a is taken down at the hypervisor (scripts/san_net.sh link) for 60 s, restored, awaited usable (bound 60 s), then its path on network b is taken down for 60 s and restored. PASS only when, per fault, every node's longest gap between completed operations is under tools/mpath_settings.sh stall-bound, zero operations errored, the kept path's write counter advanced and the removed path's did not in the second half of the window; and overall zero double grants, every acknowledged file read back with its sha256 from another node, no membership beacon below N, no shutdown/BUG/oops/hung task, 2 usable NIC-bound paths on every node at start and end, and the target's reservation keys identical at start and end.

criteria.why: Multipath exists for the moment a path is lost. A board that passes on two healthy paths says nothing about that moment, and a site told mpath works will pull a cable on day one.

criteria.requirement: When a whole storage network is lost, every node fails over to the other together and keeps working; when it returns every node reinstates it, and the cluster survives losing the other network in turn. No operation fails, no node is fenced or stops, no lock is granted twice, and every acknowledged file is intact.
criteria.detector: tests/mpath/path_fabric.sh (host-coordinated; F3 of docs/mpath-verification.md): under tests/mpath/pathload.py on every node, every node's path on storage network a is taken down at once for 60 s, restored and awaited usable on every node (bound 60 s), then the same for network b. PASS only when, per loss, every node's longest stall is under tools/mpath_settings.sh stall-bound, zero operations errored, and on every node the kept path's write counter advanced and the lost path's did not; and overall zero double grants, every acknowledged file read back by sha256 from another node, no shutdown/withdrawal/death/BUG in any node's kernel journal, 2 usable NIC-bound paths everywhere at start and end, and the target's reservation keys unchanged.

criteria.why: A node's key is registered once per path. The proof a lone survivor needs before it may reset the logical unit (that it is the only registrant) refused on that count alone, so a two-node multipath cluster could never recover a withdrawn peer.

criteria.requirement: A lock command that the target applied and whose answer the node never received is recognised when it is sent again: the lock is neither lost nor granted twice.
criteria.detector: tests/mpath/path_answer_lost.sh (host-coordinated; F9): under tests/mpath/pathload.py on every node, every frame toward the last node on path a is dropped at the hypervisor (scripts/san_net.sh mute) for 40 s while its own frames still arrive, the mute is lifted and the path reinstated, and the same is done on path b. PASS only when the victim's kernel log shows at least one resent COMPARE AND WRITE that met its own write (P-CAW-ANSWER-LOST-LANDED), per fault every node's longest stall is under tools/mpath_settings.sh stall-bound with zero errors and the kept path carrying the writes, zero double grants, every acknowledged file reads back by sha256 from another node, no shutdown/withdrawal/death/BUG, and the target's reservation keys are unchanged.
